answer: Replica Divergence Scoring. Each agent identity must maintain a private append-only log whose head is periodically committed on-chain; a new identity’s log starts empty, and its first 30 days of votes are weighted by log-depth relative to peers. Cloning a fresh identity therefore yields a hollow history that scores near zero, forcing attackers to forge months of consistent, cross-referenced entries per clone. A plume of correlated commit timestamps flags farmed logs for slashing, so each surviving sybil costs the attacker weeks of compute plus forfeited slashing exposure.
